domain.text: vmethod GitHub watcher self-attribution and suppression of orchestrator-generated events

impressions.text: The delivery merged a broad watcher fix that journals successful writes and uses journal matching, with actor checks for assignments and merges, to suppress the orchestrator’s own events while preserving activity from other sessions and people.

The worker reported 609 passing tests plus successful format, lint, typecheck, build, smoke, and knip checks; the orchestrator also reported a live smoke where own board moves were silent and a sibling-session move remained visible.

The review caught that GitHub’s field-value creator records the first writer rather than the latest, so board-move attribution was changed to rely on the session journal; the archived card’s history was unavailable, and a reproduced stale-snapshot interleaving was accepted as evidence.

The worker explicitly stopped twice for clarification or required gateway recordings, then resumed after the orchestrator answered and supplied captures; the worker did not claim to have run the remaining live acceptance.
